what_happened: Job 20261114-045625-aymy (code job: run Athena's checks in the producer loop and send failures back) failed in planning, before any code was written. The planner reached its fixed 600-second deadline without finishing a plan. The event lists no critic findings, no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered, and no partial plan or reason was kept.
cause: The planner stage has a fixed 600s wall-clock deadline. It keeps no partial plan, gives no progress signal, has no resume or retry path and records no reason. Nothing sizes a request against that deadline before planning starts. This request touches several surfaces: the producer loop, the check runner and the feedback of failures to the producer. A deadline stop therefore throws away all planning spend and leaves no diagnosis. This is at least the fifth planner-deadline failure in one day, and earlier ones did not change how later requests are planned.
other_causes: The request spans loop control, check execution and failure feedback, so it may be larger than one planning run can finish in 600s.
Earlier same-class failures today did not lead to a size check or deadline change, so each new request hit the same limit.
open_hypotheses: The planner may have been slow for a reason other than request size, such as a slow model call or reading a large code area. The event records no progress, so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out.
The 600s deadline may be too short for hard code jobs in general, not only this request.
prevention: Make planner deadline stops recoverable and diagnosable. The planner should save partial progress and a stage note at intervals. On a deadline it should hold the job as resumable with a recorded reason, not fail it. Before planning, Athena should compare the request's scope with the deadline and split or flag requests that are too large. Once one request in a class has hit the deadline, any re-ask of it should carry that failure forward and be narrowed.
proposed_request: Make the planning stage survive its 600-second deadline. When the planner reaches its deadline, Athena should keep the partial plan and a short note of what the planner was doing. It should hold the job as resumable, not failed, and record the reason. A retry should resume from the kept plan with the original request unchanged. Show the held state and the reason in athena status. Acceptance: a test with a stand-in planner that exceeds the deadline shows the job held, the partial plan kept and the reason recorded. A second test shows the retry resumes from the kept plan. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
